quotes.text: To implement this model, you create a meter to record the usage, products and prices to represent your service, a customer, and a customer subscription.
A customer’s second invoice contains their usage fees from the previous month and their license fee for the upcoming month.
The Accounts v2 API is generally available for Connect users, and in public preview for other Stripe users.
When you create a `billing_mode=flexible` subscription, Stripe excludes metered line items from the first invoice since no prior usage exists to bill.
If you represent your customers as customer-configured [Accounts](https://docs.stripe.com/api/v2/core/accounts/object.md), pass the `Account` ID to the `customer` parameter.

old_evidence.text: If your integration uses [customer-configured Accounts](https://docs.stripe.com/api/v2/core/accounts/create.md#v2_create_accounts-configuration-customer), replace `Customer` and event references in the code examples with the equivalent Accounts v2 API references.
When you create a `billing_mode=flexible` subscription, Stripe excludes metered line items from the first invoice since no prior usage exists to bill.
Because Stripe processes meter events asynchronously, upcoming invoices might not immediately reflect recently received meter events.

findings: At the same captured URL, the core flat fee plus overage flow remains a sum meter, graduated metered price with 1,000 included units, separate $100 monthly licensed price, and both prices on one subscription (new:24–30,74–82,98–114,143–154,213–258; old:25–30,73–88,116–139,142–190,219–262). The first invoice/license and second invoice/prior usage timing is an example, not proof of a successful invoice or payment.

The new capture expands the old one-line Accounts v2 caveat into an Accounts v2 creation example, a retained Customers v1 path, and customer_account versus customer subscription parameters (new:172–211,240–258; old:193–217,246–262). Accounts v2 availability is scoped: GA for Connect users, public preview for other Stripe users, with preview version for participants (new:174,189–202).

The existing source at lines 20–27 presents Node Decimal.from monetary arguments as though they define the approach; the new capture's curl example uses numeric form values (new:108–114,151–154). Existing source line 34 says the first invoice charges only the license fee under flexible mode, while new/old text excludes metered lines and also says an invoice is created only for backdated usage or pending invoice items; this prose is ambiguous for a mixed licensed plus metered subscription (new:219–223; old:225–229). Preserve the mixed subscription's upfront licensed fee separately and avoid a blanket no-first-invoice claim.

The current concept categorizes this URL's flat-fee-overages example as legacy usage-based-v1 not Meter API (wiki/concepts/stripe-usage-based-billing.md:83), despite this same page explicitly creating /v1/billing/meters, linking the metered price to recurring[meter], and submitting /v1/billing/meter_events (new:26–57,98–114,260–285; old:25–67,116–139,264–295). URL path naming does not establish a legacy aggregate_usage implementation.

The current source and index omit the new Accounts v2 and customer_account identity route, and the source's raw provenance names only the older capture (source:6–7,40–42; Stripe index:294). A coordinator update should retain the historical raw evidence while adding the pinned new capture and scoped identity facts.
substantive_changes: Expanded Accounts v2 customer-configured Account setup and scoped availability/preview version, plus an explicit Customers v1 alternative and customer_account subscription parameter (new:172–211,240–258; old:193–217,246–262).
Meter event summary prose now says to pass a customer-configured Account ID in the customer parameter (new:318); example still uses CUSTOMER_ID (new:327).

Examples switch from Node SDK and Decimal.from to curl form parameters; this changes sample syntax, not the documented meter, price, subscription, or invoice behavior (diff:28–96,129–197,217–265,354–392,407–490).
historical_claims_to_preserve: The old Node SDK examples, including Decimal.from tier amounts and customer-only subscription code, remain dated sample evidence (old:116–139,180–190,246–262), not a universal current requirement or proof that Accounts v2 was absent.

Flexible versus classic initial metered-line behavior, backdated usage/pending-item caveats, and asynchronous meter processing were present in the old raw already (old:229,315,335); do not label them new behavior.
The optional first-tier $100 flat amount places the initial license charge at period end, whereas the two-product licensed-price example charges the fee at the beginning (new:80–81; old:87–90).
conflicts: New:64 calls the metered rate $0.04 per hundred units, while new:79 and tiers[1][unit_amount_decimal]=4 at new:111–113 express $0.04 per unit above 1,000. The same conflict appears in old:73 versus old:88,134–136. Avoid asserting the per-hundred rate without qualification.

Concept wiki/concepts/stripe-usage-based-billing.md:83,86 calls this legacy usage-based-v1 not Meter API and Decimal.from required; both conflict with the meter-creation/event API in the captured guide and the new curl numeric tier values (new:26–57,98–114,279–285). Reciprocal concept/source correction is needed.

The guide's broad new:9 says an end-of-month invoice combines the flat fee and overage, while its specific two-product example new:80 says the next invoice combines prior-month overage with upcoming-month license. New:223's invoice-only-if-backdated-or-pending statement is ambiguous for this mixed-price case. Preserve the specific timing and qualify invoice creation to metered-only context rather than extending it to licensed charges.

The new Accounts v2 subscription and event summary examples use customer_account or Account ID (new:245,318), but the meter-event sample still passes CUSTOMER_ID (new:283) and the summary curl uses CUSTOMER_ID (new:327). Do not infer the event example demonstrates an Account v2 payload end-to-end.
unresolved_questions: Does the new raw's $0.04 per hundred units sentence at line 64 reflect a documentation typo? The Dashboard tier and API tier amount indicate per unit; no live execution was performed.

How should the guide's line 223 invoice-only-if-backdated-or-pending caveat be interpreted for the shown mixed licensed and metered subscription? This capture does not demonstrate an invoice creation result.
What exact meter-event customer mapping is required for the Accounts v2 variant? The guide does not show an Account v2 meter-event example, despite its subscription and summary variants.

answers.Q1: For https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/usage-based-v1/use-cases/flat-fee-and-overages, [[source-stripe-usage-based-billing-flat-fee-overages]] should describe a sum meter, a graduated metered overage price with 1,000 included units, and a separate licensed $100 monthly price on one subscription; second-cycle billing combines prior usage with the next license fee (new:24–30,74–82,98–114,213–258; old:25–30,87–90,219–262). The new capture adds customer-configured Account creation and customer_account alongside Customers v1, scoped to Accounts v2 GA for Connect or preview for other users (new:172–211,240–258; old:193–217). Flexible/classic first metered-line behavior and async usage lag remain state limits, not observed payment outcomes (new:223,306,322; old:229,315,335).
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/billing/subscriptions/usage-based-v1/use-cases/flat-fee-and-overages, [[source-stripe-usage-based-billing-flat-fee-overages]] needs a source update chiefly for the expanded Accounts v2 identity path, preview/version bounds, and Account ID event-summary guidance (new:172–211,240–258,318; old:195,246–262,331–349). Node-to-curl and list formatting changes are presentational; retain the old SDK samples as dated examples, not current required syntax. Correct the concept's claim that this guide is non-Meter API, since both captures create a meter and send events (new:26–57,279–285; old:25–67,281–295). Warn about the preexisting per-hundred versus per-unit rate conflict and the mixed-subscription first-invoice ambiguity (new:64,79,223; old:73,88,229), without asserting account eligibility or invoice/payment finality from sample code.
